Heart Disease Prediction

From raw clinical data to an evaluated XGBoost model and a Flask application with explanations, batch scoring and prediction history.

The question

Can a model predict heart disease risk from clinical features while giving users a clear view of the factors behind each prediction? I treated this as both a modeling problem and a product problem: the evaluation needed to be sound, and the result needed to be usable beyond a notebook.

Data & model comparison

I worked with the UCI Heart Disease dataset. Exploratory data analysis and statistical hypothesis testing informed feature selection. I trained and compared Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM and XGBoost, then selected XGBoost based on the evaluation results.

UCI data→Explore & select→Compare 4 models→Tune XGBoost→Explain & serve

Validation & explainability

GridSearchCV tuned the selected model. I checked its behavior with k-fold cross-validation and compared it with voting and stacking ensembles. SHAP analysis makes individual predictions more interpretable by showing which input features most influenced a score.

84% accuracy · 0.87 ROC-AUC

Reported model evaluation results on the UCI dataset.

Delivery

I packaged the workflow as a Flask web application with user authentication, CSV upload for batch scoring and SQLite-backed prediction history. That connects preprocessing, inference and explanation to an interface someone can use.

This is a portfolio modeling system evaluated on a public dataset. Clinical use would require external validation, medical review and further safety checks.
